Okay, so I'm trying to figure out why balsam fir trees in Maine have similar needle lengths. The options given are about sunlight, closeness to the ocean, inherited information in seeds, or insects eating the needles. I remember from biology that many traits in plants are influenced by genetics, so I'm leaning towards the inherited information in seeds being the main reason. But I need to make sure I'm not missing something.

First, I think about how plants grow. They have different needs, like sunlight, water, and nutrients, which can affect their size and shape. But balsam fir trees are all in Maine, so maybe they all get similar amounts of sunlight and water. That could make their needle lengths similar because of environmental factors. But then again, if it's genetics, all the trees would have the same genetic makeup, leading to similar needle lengths regardless of their environment.

I also recall that when trees are propagated from seeds, the genetic information from the parent tree is passed on. So if all the balsam fir trees in Maine are from the same stock, their needles would naturally be the same length because they have the same DNA. This makes sense because even if they're in the same environment, genetic factors can determine their physical traits more consistently than environmental factors alone.

On the other hand, the other options don't seem as strong. The amount of sunlight they receive might vary a bit, but if they're all in similar forest conditions, it's probably not the main reason. Being close to the ocean could affect humidity or salt levels, but again, I don't think that's the primary factor for needle length. Insects eating the needles would affect the health of the tree, but it's not directly causing the needles to be a specific length.

So, putting it all together, the most plausible answer is that the similar needle lengths are due to the inherited information inside the seeds, which is a genetic factor. This would explain why all the trees have the same needle length, even if they're in the same environment.
